rulings.opponent: Rhode Island (ECAC New England Regional final, Providence Civic Center)

sources.quote: UConn Five Stymies Rhode Island, 58‐50 (published Sunday, March 4, 1979)
DePaul Five Upsets Notre Dame, 76‐72 (Saturday Mar. 3 paper carries Friday-night games; no UConn-URI story)
3/1 Rhode Island ! N37 L, 71-75
ECAC New England Regional M 1 PCC Connecticut L 74-91
Connecticut won the ECAC New England title by beating Boston College 91-74 and knocking off Rhode Island 58-50.

rulings.note: Both semifinals (UConn-BC, URI-Holy Cross) were Thursday Mar. 1 per BC's and Holy Cross's own records. The NYT game story on the final ran in the Sunday Mar. 4 paper, while the Saturday Mar. 3 paper (which carried Friday-night games such as DePaul-Notre Dame) had none, so the final was Saturday Mar. 3. Record book (3/3) is right; app (3/2) is wrong.

sources.quote: Jan. 10, 1980 * 71-83 L Hartford, Conn.
1979-80 ... J 10 A Connecticut* L 71-83 / J 12 A Fordham W 60-47
UConn schedule (page n172): "Boston Coll.* .... J9"; BC schedule (page n170): "Connecticut .... J9" (preseason, 'subject to change')

rulings.note: BC's own record book gives Jan. 10, 1980 (a Thursday) in two separate places: the series list and the 1979-80 game list. That matches UConn's record book. Against it, both teams' preseason schedules in Street & Smith's 1979-80 yearbook list the game for Wednesday Jan. 9, which matches SR/the app and fits UConn's usual Wed/Sat home pattern that season. So either the game was moved a day, or both record books are off. I found no game report from the time: the NYT Jan. 10/11 roundup headlines don't mention it, and the Courant, Globe, BC Heights and UConn Daily Campus for that week were unreachable or not digitized. BC's series list also gives the site as Hartford, which is doubtful: the Hartford Civic Center didn't reopen until Feb. 1980 (UConn's first game back there was 2/9 vs URI), and UConn's book marks this as a plain Storrs home game. Leaning record-book date (1/10). Upgrade to high only with a newspaper.

Feb 14 (Mon) Big East * at Connecticut Storrs, Conn. W, 77-60
2/14/1983 | ESPN | W | 77-60 | at | Connecticut | Hartford, CT | Hartford Civic Ctr. | 14,454 | Three with 15
the Blizzard of '83 that dumped more than 2 feet of snow along the Atlantic Coast late last week

rulings.note: A UPI game story from the time says the game was played Monday night (Feb. 14). Georgetown's site agrees: Mon Feb 14, though it lists the site as Storrs. hoyabasketball also agrees and adds ESPN and Hartford Civic Center, 14,454. The rb's 2/12 (a Saturday) was most likely the pre-blizzard schedule date: the Northeast blizzard of Feb. 11-12, 1983 postponed events that weekend (NYT Feb. 12 'Snowstorm Puts Off Events', Feb. 13 'Storm Buries Schedule'). The same knock-on shows in the next game: see bonus ruling 1983-StJohns-date. App (2/14) is right; record book (2/12) is wrong.

rulings.opponent: Utah (Utah Classic, Salt Lake City, Dec. 8, 1979)
rulings.truth: Confirmed. Utah's star forward Danny Vranes was ruled ineligible over Ottawa University extension-course credit, and Utah forfeited the five early-season non-conference wins he played in. Those five can only be Utah State 12/4, Cal St. Fullerton 12/7, Connecticut 12/8, Nevada 12/12 and Pacific 12/15, so the UConn game (lost 66-73 on the court) is a UConn forfeit win. Caveat: Utah's own current record book does not reflect the forfeits.

sources.quote: a Western Athletic Conference committee has ruled that Vranes was ineligible for five games he played in ... Utah likely will have to forfeit five of its early season victories, all against non-conference opponents. (AP, BYU Daily Universe, Fri Jan 11, 1980)
Utah, while denying wrong doing on the part of its player, forfeited five basketball victories. (BYU Daily Universe, Tue Jan 29, 1980)

Dec. 22: Immediately before the University of Utah basketball team's 71-69 upset of national champion-to-be Louisville ... Utah ruled Vranes ineligible. (SI, May 19, 1980, reprinted in Hillis v. Stephen F. Austin cert. filing)
CONNECTICUT ... 12/08/1979 W 73-66 Salt Lake City; 1979-80 OVERALL RECORD • 18-10

rulings.note: Why UConn must be one of the five: Utah went 5-4 in the nine games before Vranes was held out on Dec. 22. Its only wins in that stretch were USU, CSUF, UConn, Nevada and Pacific, all non-conference, which matches 'five ... early season victories, all against non-conference opponents.' AP's Jan. 9-11 story says forfeits were 'likely'. AP's Jan. 29 roundup on the transcript scandal states them as done. Utah's current record book still shows the UConn game as a 73-66 Utah win and the season as 18-10, so the forfeit appears only in UConn's (winner's) books. Correction to the prompt's framing: the ineligibility was academic (unaccepted summer correspondence-course credit), not a recruiting or eligibility-year issue.
